newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end up as players optimistic for growth.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end up as players optimistic for growth.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Thursday for the second consecutive session as investors were confident the economy's strong growth prospects would result in solid company profits, brokers said.
The market was expected to edge up Friday, they added.
Thursday, the General Index IGRA rose 1.76 percent to 2,130.3 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index ISEL gained 1.22 percent to 3,053.5 points.
In a total of 2,100 trades, volume was 45.5 million soles ($17.2 million), brokers said.

Wednesday's upward momentum when foreign funds entered the market late in the session carried into Thursday's trade, as players recognized Tuesday's sharp fall had only served to set new price floors, they said.

"The market found a new floor and investors are now expected to focus on mining and industrial shares because zinc prices continue rising and the improved economy will show in company profits," Bruno Calle of local brokerage Argenta said.
Benchmark Telefonica ended up 1.18 percent at 6.84 soles on modest volume of 451,000 shares.
Peru's largest brewery group Union de Cervecerias Peruanas Backus y Johnston SA gained 0.78 percent to 2.60 soles on strong volume of 1.9 million shares.

Atacocha -- the leading polymetallic miner that has seen most gains in the mining sector's bull run -- bucked Thursday's trend to continue its own technical correction, plunging 11.29 percent to close at 2.20 soles on volume of 795,000 shares.
